title: Inner Preparation Computation
statement: Let $C,e$ be natural numbers, let $\mathrm{mode}$ be Boolean, and let $f$ map finite Boolean words to finite Boolean words. Suppose that for every Boolean word $y$, $|f(y)|\le C(|y|+1)^e$. Let $x,b$ be Boolean words, let $p$ be a natural number, and suppose that $b$ is empty or its last bit is true. Let $v$ assign natural numbers to fourteen registers, each at most $8(2C+3)(|\langle\langle x,b\rangle,\mathrm{bits}(p)\rangle|+1)^{e+1}$. Suppose register $3$ equals $2|\langle x,b\rangle|$, register $4$ equals $4|x|+4$, register $5$ equals $p$, and registers $6,7,10,11,12,13$ are all zero. Starting in the inner-preparation state with these register values, no result yet, and input $\langle\langle x,b\rangle,\mathrm{bits}(p)\rangle$, the counter machine halts with result true precisely when $p<|\langle f(x),b\rangle|$ if $\mathrm{mode}$ is true; otherwise its result is the bit at index $p$ of $\langle f(x),b\rangle$, or false if that index is beyond the end. Before halting, every configuration satisfies the machine's step-validity condition, and all register values remain within the stated bound.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ maps Boolean words to Boolean words
$b$ is empty or ends in true
$v$ assigns natural numbers to fourteen registers
Every value of $v$ is at most $8(2C+3)(|\langle\langle x,b\rangle,\mathrm{bits}(p)\rangle|+1)^{e+1}$
replaced:
Let $C,e,B$ be natural numbers, let $\mathrm{mode}$ be a Boolean flag, let $f$ map bit
strings to bit strings, and suppose $|f(y)|\le C(|y|+1)^e$ for every bit string $y$. Let
$x,b$ be bit strings, let $p$ be a natural number, and suppose the last bit of $b$ is
true whenever $b$ is nonempty. Let $v$ assign a natural number to each of the 14
registers, with every register value at most $8(2C+3)(|\langle\langle
x,b\rangle,\mathrm{bits}(p)\rangle|+1)^{e+1}$. Suppose register $3$ is twice the length
of the encoding of $x$ paired with $b$, register $4$ is $4|x|+4$, register $5$ is $p$,
and registers $6,7,10,11,12,13$ are all zero. Starting in the inner-preparation state,
the specified counter machine halts with the answer that is true exactly when $p$ is
less than the length of the encoding of $f(x)$ paired with $b$ if $\mathrm{mode}$ is
true; otherwise its answer is the bit at position $p$ in that encoding, using false when
that position is beyond the end. Throughout the run, its step-validity condition holds
and every register remains within the stated bound.
